title: Manager break corrections are wrongly refused when a session has more than one break.
scenario: Omar takes a tea break from 10:00 to 10:10 and a lunch break from 13:00 to 13:30. Tom tries to correct the lunch start to 13:05, but the system refuses because 13:05 is after the end of the tea break. Correcting the tea break's end to 10:12 is also refused because it is before the lunch start. Tom cannot fix break times, so Omar's paid minutes stay wrong.
test_needed: A session with two break pairs: correcting the second BREAK_START to a time inside the second break succeeds.

owner_question.question: Omar took a tea break and a lunch break. Tom needs to move the lunch start by five minutes. What should happen?
options: Allow it: only check against that break's own end and against clock in and clock out
Allow it, and also block any overlap between the two breaks
Keep today's behaviour: refuse the correction

title: Anyone at the counter kiosk can start or end a break for a locum or cross-site worker without any PIN.
scenario: Sara, a locum with a confirmed shift, clocks in by phone QR and has no membership PIN at Tom's pharmacy. The kiosk staff list shows her worker ID, and anyone at the counter (for example Mia) can tap break start for Sara with no PIN asked. Sara's unpaid break time begins without her knowing. Nadia, covering from Tom's other pharmacy, has the same problem because only a local membership PIN is checked.
test_needed: A break START from the kiosk for a clocked-in worker with no local membership PIN is refused unless that worker proves who they are.

owner_question.question: Sara is clocked in at Tom's pharmacy and has no kiosk PIN there. Mia taps 'start break' for Sara on the counter kiosk. What should happen?
options: Refuse: the worker must confirm with their own PIN or app
Allow it but tell Sara and flag it for Tom to review
Keep today's behaviour: allow it with no check

title: A repeated kiosk PIN submit flips the worker's clock state instead of being treated as a retry.
scenario: Omar types his PIN at Tom's kiosk and presses Clock, but the screen lags (or the kiosk resends after a slow network), so the same request arrives twice. The first request clocks him in. The second one sees an open session and clocks him straight back out, leaving a session of almost zero minutes while Omar thinks he is on the clock. The same thing happens at clock-out: a repeated request starts a new session that stays open overnight, so Tom's timesheet shows hours Omar never worked.
test_needed: Send POST kiosk/pin-clock/ twice within 5 seconds with the same PIN and check that exactly one CLOCK_IN exists and the session is still open.

owner_question.question: Omar presses Clock twice within a few seconds at Tom's kiosk. What should happen?
options: The second press within 30 seconds counts as the same action; Omar stays clocked in
The kiosk asks Omar to confirm before clocking out someone who clocked in under a minute ago
Keep today's behaviour: each press flips Omar between clocked in and clocked out

title: The kiosk staff lookup reveals staff names and masked emails by guessable number, and sends setup emails without a dedicated rate limit.
scenario: Anyone standing at the paired counter tablet in Tom's pharmacy can type 1, 2, 3 and so on into the Staff ID box. For Omar, Ali, Mia, and also Nadia at Tom's other pharmacy, the kiosk shows the full name, account number and a partly hidden email. Unknown numbers get a different 'not found' answer, so every staff member in the group can be listed. Anyone who has no PIN yet (for example a new starter like Jack) gets a setup-code email on every probe. The PIN clock screen deliberately gives one generic error so this cannot happen, but the lookup screen undoes that.
test_needed: Using one device token, look up a known staff ID and an unknown one and assert both answers look the same with no name or email; then assert repeated lookups are rate-limited like the PIN screen.

owner_question.question: Someone at Tom's counter tablet types Staff ID numbers one after another. What should the kiosk show them?
options: Nothing that names anyone: the same neutral 'enter your PIN or check your email' answer for every number, rate-limited
Show names only for staff of this pharmacy, never staff from Tom's other pharmacies, and rate-limit lookups
Keep today's behaviour: show the name and partly hidden email so staff can confirm it is them

title: The kiosk login check also accepts the stored token text as-is, so the scrambled copy saved in the database works as a kiosk token.
scenario: Kiosk tokens are saved only in scrambled (hashed) form so that a leaked database or backup can't be used to sign in a kiosk. But the login check also accepts a token that matches the saved text exactly. So anyone who sees the saved value for Tom's front-counter kiosk (in a backup, an admin screen or a support export) can send it as the token and act as that kiosk: show sign-in QR codes, look up staff and clock people in. Nothing hashes old plain-text tokens, so this extra check is permanent.
test_needed: Activate a kiosk, read its saved hash from the database, call authenticate_kiosk_device with that hash and assert it returns None.

owner_question.question: If someone gets a copy of Tom's database backup, should the kiosk token values in it be enough to run Tom's counter kiosk?
options: No: hash the old plain-text tokens once and accept only real tokens from then on
No: make old unhashed kiosks pair again, then drop the extra check
Keep today's behaviour so very old kiosks keep working

title: Anyone with one active membership can pull any pharmacy's staff into a custom group and harvest their names and emails.
scenario: Sara has one active membership somewhere. She creates a custom group chat and lists membership numbers from many pharmacies, including Nadia at Tom's other pharmacy. Each person is added with no check that Sara shares a pharmacy with them. Sara then opens her chat participants list and sees each person's name, email, photo and job type, and can message all of them.
test_needed: Sara creates a group with Nadia's membership id from an unrelated pharmacy; expect 400/403 and no Participant row for Nadia.

owner_question.question: When Sara builds a custom group chat, whom should she be allowed to add?
options: Only people she shares an accepted pharmacy membership with
Only people she already has a DM or shift with
Anyone on the platform (keep today's behaviour)

title: A shift checkout without selected offers charges one fee but confirms every worker waiting for payment.
scenario: Tom's shift has three slots, each with a worker waiting on payment. If checkout is started without naming offers or slots, Stripe charges a single fee. When it is paid, all three workers are confirmed. With slots named, two workers waiting on the same slot are also both confirmed for one fee. ChemistTasker is underpaid for each extra worker.
test_needed: Shift with 3 awaiting offers on 3 slots: POST charge-fulfillment with {} and expect a 400 or quantity 3, not quantity 1 that finalizes 3.

owner_question.question: Tom pays the fee once while three workers are waiting on his shift. What should happen?
options: Require Tom to pick the workers, and charge one fee per worker
Charge for all waiting workers automatically
One fee confirms everyone (keep today's behaviour)

title: An organisation's free trial depends on which org admin clicks pay, so a newly joined admin makes every shift free.
scenario: Lina's organisation has been on ChemistTasker for a year. A newly created org admin account, under 30 days old, pays a shift fee for Tom's pharmacy, and the shift is confirmed free as a 'free trial'. This can be repeated with each new admin account. The same shift costs money if a chief admin or Lina pays instead.
test_needed: Org created long ago, new ORG_ADMIN joined today pays fulfilment; expect PAYMENT_REQUIRED, not FREE_TRIAL.

owner_question.question: Lina's year-old organisation adds a new admin, who pays a shift fee. Should it be free?
options: No: the trial follows the organisation's start date
Trial follows the first org admin only
Yes: it follows whoever pays (keep today's behaviour)

title: Organisation billing falls back to the pharmacy owner's personal subscription for viewing, seat purchases and subscriber status.
scenario: Tom has his own active subscription, and his pharmacy belongs to Lina's organisation, which has none. Lina's org billing page shows Tom's subscription and its payment-provider ids as the organisation's. When Lina buys extra seats, the checkout runs on Tom's payment customer, and the seats may land on the organisation's record without any base plan.
test_needed: Org without subscription, owner with active one: ORG_ADMIN GET subscription returns inactive/none, and seat purchase is refused.

owner_question.question: Tom pays for his own plan and his pharmacy is in Lina's organisation. What should Lina's org billing show?
options: Only the organisation's own subscription (none)
Tom's plan, read-only, with no seat changes
Tom's plan, fully manageable (keep today's behaviour)

title: Deleting the owner's user account deletes all their shift payment records.
scenario: Tom paid fulfilment fees and penalties, including fees paid for organisation pharmacies, which are recorded under the pharmacy owner. If Tom's account is deleted, every payment record tied to him is deleted too. ChemistTasker loses the financial history it needs for refunds, disputes and tax records.
test_needed: Delete a user with ShiftPayment rows; expect the payments to remain (protected or owner set null).

owner_question.question: Tom deletes his account after paying shift fees. What should happen to those payment records?
options: Keep them, with Tom's identity anonymised
Block account deletion while payment records exist
Delete them with the account (keep today's behaviour)

title: Any chat member can rewrite who is in a room through the plain room update, skipping the creator/admin check and the community-chat block.
scenario: Mia, an ordinary assistant at Tom's pharmacy, edits the pharmacy's community chat through the standard room-edit call. She removes every member except the creator and adds Sara, an outside locum, by picking any active membership on the platform. Sara can now read the whole community chat history through the message list, even though she has no role at Tom's pharmacy. The same call also lets a non-admin member of a custom group rename it or remove the other members. The dedicated group-edit path would have refused both.
test_needed: As a non-admin, non-creator staff member, PATCH /rooms/<community_chat_id>/ with participants=[outsider_membership_id]. Expect 403, no new Participant row for the outsider, and no change to existing participants.

owner_question.question: Mia is a regular staff member, not a chat admin. She tries to change the members of Tom's pharmacy community chat, or of a custom group Omar created. What should happen?
options: Refuse: only the group creator or a group admin (or a pharmacy admin with comms rights, for community chats) can change members or the title
Let Mia add people from her own pharmacy only, and never remove anyone
Keep today's behaviour: any member can change the member list and title

title: Worker dashboard exposes community shift IDs and dates to staff outside the vacancy's audience.
scenario: Ben is Tom's favourite locum and should only be offered favourite-locum shifts, not Tom's internal staff vacancies. The pharmacist dashboard counts and returns a FULL_PART_TIME vacancy to Ben as a community opportunity, including its identifier and date. The normal worker shift listing correctly excludes it.
test_needed: Ben is an accepted LOCUM member only. Tom creates a FULL_PART_TIME internal pharmacist shift; GET /api/v1/dashboard/pharmacist/?workspace=internal&pharmacy_id=... must exclude its ID and count; Omar (accepted FULL_TIME) must see it.

owner_question.question: Should favourite locum Ben see counts, dates or IDs of Tom's internal FULL_PART_TIME staff vacancies?
options: No: use the same audience filter as internal shift browsing
Only show aggregated counts, not identifiers or dates
Yes: keep current community opportunity listing

title: Mobile dashboards label all-time drafted invoice value as this month's income.
scenario: Sara issued an invoice in January, then another in October. The October pharmacist dashboard labels the sum of both invoices 'Total Income This Month', and even counts unsent draft invoices. The backend returns all-time billed amounts without a date or paid-status filter; the other-staff mobile dashboard uses the same label.
test_needed: Sara has an old invoice, this-month sent invoice and an unsent draft; load pharmacist dashboard and assert a clearly defined monthly income metric excludes last month and drafts, while all-time billed metric remains separately labelled.

owner_question.question: What should Sara's 'Income This Month' tile count?
options: Only money actually received during the current calendar month
Invoices issued this month, labelled 'This Month Invoiced'
All-time invoice totals, but relabel them accurately

title: Ethical stock imports can still be committed after the inventory write feature is switched off.
scenario: Tom stages an ethical stock CSV while the inventory feature is available. An administrator disables ethical inventory writes to stop unsafe stock changes. Tom can still invoke the import-commit endpoint, which changes stock quantities and creates stock-movement records without checking the disabled feature flag.
test_needed: Stage a valid import as a verified entitled owner with ETHICAL_INVENTORY_ENABLED=True; disable it before POST /api/v1/ethical/inventory/imports/{pk}/commit/; expect 503 and no EthicalStockLot/Movement changes. Positive flag-true commit still succeeds.

owner_question.question: When ethical inventory writes are disabled, should a previously staged import still update stock?
options: No: block every stock-mutating endpoint including commit
Allow viewing staged rows but require explicit re-enable to commit
Allow previously staged imports to commit after writes are disabled

title: Editing an ethical draft can reassign it to another owner's pharmacy and another product without destination authorization.
scenario: Tom delegates preparation of his ethical listing to Omar. Omar edits that DRAFT with Nadia's unrelated pharmacy identifier and another approved product. The update saves the reassignment without proving Omar can manage Nadia's pharmacy or that he is approved for the replacement product. Nadia's stock workflow can then contain Tom's unauthorized listing.
test_needed: Create a draft owned by pharmacy A. As authorized A preparer, PATCH its pharmacy to unrelated B and product to unapproved S8; assert 403/400 and no owner/product/lot/audience changes. Valid description-only update remains allowed.

owner_question.question: May Omar move a draft ethical medicine listing from Tom's premises to Nadia's unrelated premises without the destination owner authorising it?
options: No; immutable pharmacy and product with fresh draft required for material changes
Only with explicit authorization from both pharmacy owners and new product policy checks
Yes; leave the existing draft PATCH behavior

title: Concurrent identical marketplace enquiries can persist duplicate negotiations before the idempotency receipt fails.
scenario: Sara sends an enquiry to Tom's listing twice at the same instant. Both requests see no prior idempotency receipt and create separate exchanges, after which the second hits a unique receipt constraint and returns an error. Tom can receive two negotiations for one enquiry.
test_needed: Concurrently submit identical enquiry UUIDs using PostgreSQL and verify exactly one exchange and one receipt, with repeat-safe response.

owner_question.question: What should happen if Sara accidentally submits her marketplace enquiry to Tom twice simultaneously?
options: Create one negotiation and replay its outcome
Create one negotiation and safely reject the duplicate
Create two negotiations with a server error (current race)

title: Revoked invitation sender continues receiving membership response notifications containing staff identities.
scenario: Lina invites Sara to Tom's pharmacy but subsequently loses her organisation membership and staff-management authority. When Sara responds or leaves, Lina remains a notification recipient through the original inviter link and receives Sara's name and email.
test_needed: After revoking Lina's organisation/pharmacy authority, make Sara accept/leave. Lina receives no email or in-app notification; valid managers still receive it.

owner_question.question: Should former manager Lina continue receiving Sara's membership notifications after her access is revoked?
options: No, recheck recipient authority for each event
Only the initial invitation response
Yes, retain all inviter notifications after removal

title: Authenticated workers can create applications against expired or unauthorised invitation links by calling the generic applications endpoint.
scenario: Sara has no valid invitation to Tom's pharmacy. She obtains or guesses a numeric invite-link identifier and sends her details to the membership-applications API directly. The create endpoint only requires authentication and its serializer accepts the link ID without checking active status or expiry, bypassing the secure magic-link application route.
test_needed: As unrelated authenticated Sara, POST /api/v1/membership-applications/ with a valid old or disabled invite_link integer, matching her email/DOB/role. Expect refusal and zero application creation; valid UUID magic-link flow must succeed.

owner_question.question: May Sara apply to Tom's pharmacy using the internal numeric ID of an expired or revoked invitation?
options: No, all application creation must require a valid active token
Allow only when Tom explicitly re-enables the invitation
Yes, the numeric ID is sufficient

title: A pharmacy administrator can permanently delete pending and decided membership application review records through generic DELETE.
scenario: Lina is authorised to review applications for Tom's pharmacy. After deciding an application, she calls DELETE on the application detail endpoint. The default ModelViewSet destroys the application and its submitted snapshot and reviewer decision, removing the employment decision audit trail instead of recording an archival state.
test_needed: As scoped manager attempt DELETE on approved, rejected and pending applications; require 405/403 or audited soft-archive, preserving submitted/decision history. Verify positive review/approve/reject remains functional.

owner_question.question: Should Lina be allowed to permanently delete historic membership applications and decisions?
options: No, retain review history and permit only audited archive
Only permit irreversible deletion by an audited super-admin workflow
Yes, ordinary managers may delete application history

title: AHPRA suspension notices expose an employee's regulatory status to region administrators outside their assigned pharmacies.
scenario: Sara works at Tom's pharmacy and her AHPRA registration is suspended. Grace is a region administrator in the same organisation but assigned only to Nadia's different pharmacy. The suspension notifier delivers Sara's name, pharmacy affiliation and registration status to Grace despite her lacking permission to manage Tom's pharmacy.
test_needed: Create two pharmacies in one organisation; Sara is at A, Grace REGION_ADMIN assigned only B. Trigger Sara AHPRA suspension and assert Grace receives no in-app/email status, while authorized A managers do.

owner_question.question: Should region administrator Grace receive Sara's AHPRA suspension details when Sara works at a pharmacy Grace cannot manage?
options: No; deliver only to managers scoped to Sara's pharmacy
Send a generic staffing alert without identity or regulatory detail
Yes; all regional administrators in the organisation receive detailed suspension notices

title: Ordinary pharmacy workers can list private hub groups and obtain their full membership rosters without joining them.
scenario: Mia works at Tom's pharmacy but is not a member of its restricted managers' group. Mia requests all pharmacy groups with include_members=true. The group list is authorized only against Mia's general pharmacy membership and exposes the managers' group name, description and member details, despite group-specific access forbidding her.
test_needed: Create private manager group G at pharmacy A and ordinary nonmember Mia at A; GET /api/v1/hub/community-groups/?pharmacy_id=A&include_members=true must not return G or its members. Authorized group member and managers still see permitted details.

owner_question.question: Should Mia see the names, descriptions and member rosters of private groups at Tom's pharmacy when she is not a group member?
options: No, hide restricted groups from nonmembers
Show group titles only without rosters or descriptions
Yes, every pharmacy member can view complete group rosters

title: Hub group PATCH can reassign an existing group to an unrelated pharmacy without checking destination tenant authority.
scenario: Tom administers a community group at his own pharmacy. He edits it and includes Nadia's unrelated pharmacy identifier. The group update authorizes only the original group and accepts the serializer's writable pharmacy field, moving the group and its existing memberships into a different pharmacy context without Nadia's consent.
test_needed: As Tom, manage group G in pharmacy A; PATCH G with pharmacy=B owned by unrelated Nadia. Assert mutation rejected and group pharmacy, member links and posts remain in A. Valid same-pharmacy description change succeeds.

owner_question.question: May Tom move an existing group and its posts into Nadia's unrelated pharmacy using an ordinary group edit?
options: No, pharmacy ownership of a group is immutable
Only through an explicit, audited two-party transfer workflow
Yes, source manager authorization is sufficient

title: Editing a poll, even just to fix a typo in the question, deletes every vote already cast.
scenario: Tom posts a poll in his pharmacy hub and Omar, Ali and Mia vote. Tom opens Edit to fix a spelling mistake in the question and saves. Web and mobile always resend the option list, so the server deletes all votes and rebuilds the options. The poll goes back to zero votes and nobody is warned.
test_needed: PATCH a poll that has votes, sending the same option labels and a new question; assert the votes and vote counts are kept.

owner_question.question: Tom edits a poll that Omar, Ali and Mia have already voted on. What should happen to their votes?
options: Votes are kept when the options are unchanged; only changed options lose their votes
Options are locked once anyone has voted; only the question can change
Keep today's behaviour: every edit clears all votes, but show Tom a warning first

title: Tagging teammates fails when editing a post, and when a new post has a file and exactly one tag.
scenario: Tom edits his pharmacy hub post on mobile to tag Omar and gets 'Unable to determine post scope for tagging', so the edit is refused. Separately, Tom writes a new post on web with a photo and tags only Omar. The upload turns the single tag into plain text instead of a list, so the post is rejected. It works only with no attachment or with two or more tags.
test_needed: PATCH an existing pharmacy post with tagged_member_ids=[staff id], and multipart-POST a post with one attachment and one tagged_member_ids value; both should return 200/201.

owner_question.question: Tom edits a post to tag Omar, or posts a photo tagging only Omar. What should happen?
options: Both work and Omar is notified
Tags can only be added when a post is first created; the edit screen hides tagging
Keep today's behaviour (both requests fail with an error)

title: Comment alerts with the comment text still go to a post's author after they lose access to that private hub.
scenario: Nadia wrote a post in her pharmacy's private hub and later left that pharmacy. Mia comments on the old post. Nadia's account is still active, so she gets an alert with the first 280 characters of Mia's internal comment and a link to a hub she can no longer open. The only check is whether the author's account is active, not whether they can still see the hub.
test_needed: Make the post author's membership inactive, comment as another member, and assert the former author gets no notification.

owner_question.question: Nadia left the pharmacy, but her old hub post gets a new comment from Mia. Should Nadia hear about it?
options: No alert once she can no longer see that hub
An alert with no comment text (just 'someone commented')
Keep today's behaviour (alert includes the comment text)

title: The editorial seed command has no production guard and changes admin access, live articles and comments under real users' names.
scenario: An operator runs the seed command on the live server, maybe after copying it from a setup note. If the hard-coded author emails do not exist, the very first account in the database (for example Tom) silently becomes a full content administrator, with publishing, invitation and moderation powers. Live launch guides are overwritten with localhost cover images, and made-up 'news' plus sample comments and reactions are posted under real members' accounts. Readers see fake regulatory news and comments that real pharmacists never wrote.
test_needed: Run seed_editorial_content with production settings (DEBUG off, not public_hub.test_settings) and assert that it raises CommandError and makes no ContentAdministrator, Article or Comment changes.

owner_question.question: If someone runs the editorial seed command on the live site, what should happen to Tom's account, the published guides and the comments shown to readers?
options: Refuse to run outside local/test settings, like the hub preview seed
Allow it on live only with an explicit --i-know flag, and never grant admin or post comments as real users
Keep today's behaviour (seed runs anywhere)

title: After a board report is resolved, the same user can never report that talent post or job shift again, yet is told the report was received.
scenario: Sara reports a job board shift Tom posted, and a moderator resolves it without hiding it. Tom later edits the shift description into something abusive. When Sara reports it again she sees 'Report received', but the system only finds her old resolved report, so nothing new reaches the moderators.
test_needed: Create a BoardReport by Sara, mark it resolved, have Sara POST the report again, and assert that an unresolved report now appears in the moderation queue.

owner_question.question: Sara's report on a job shift was dismissed, and the shift then changed. When she reports it again, what should happen?
options: A new open report reaches the moderators
Sara's old report reopens with her new reason
Keep today's behaviour (silently ignored, but she is told it was received)

title: Concurrent referral claims can award the same referral twice
scenario: Tom shares his friend referral with Sara. Sara has a verified account and submits the same claim twice at the same time. Both claims can succeed, giving Tom two 100-Pill rewards for referring Sara once; the extra credit can pay for shifts.
test_needed: Submit two concurrent first claims by verified Sara for Tom's same referral code, synchronizing their initial lookups; assert one claimed referral and one 100-Pill credit.

owner_question.question: When Sara submits Tom's same referral claim twice simultaneously, what should Tom receive?
options: One reward, with both submissions resolving to the same referral
One reward, with the duplicate submission rejected
Two rewards (keep today's behaviour)

title: Manual rostering allows staff to fill a pharmacist vacancy without pharmacist eligibility
scenario: Tom submits a manual roster assignment putting Ali into a pharmacist vacancy. Ali's accepted technician membership satisfies the checks, so the assignment succeeds without checking that Ali can perform pharmacist work.
test_needed: Manually assign accepted technician Ali to a pharmacist vacancy and assert rejection with no assignment created.

owner_question.question: When Tom manually puts Ali into a pharmacist vacancy, what should happen?
options: Reject because Ali is not a pharmacist
Require Tom to change the vacancy to technician work first
Allow Ali to fill the pharmacist vacancy (keep today's behaviour)

title: One claimed slot prevents claims on every remaining free slot
scenario: Tom posts two independently claimable pharmacist dates. Omar claims the first date, then tries to claim the second. The second claim is refused because the shift already has an assignment, although that date remains free.
test_needed: Claim one slot in a non-single-user shift, then claim another free slot and assert success.

owner_question.question: After Omar claims the first of Tom's independently claimable dates, what should happen to the second?
options: Keep the second date available for claims
Require Tom to offer the remaining date manually
Block all further claims on the shift (keep today's behaviour)

title: Recurring vacancies disappear from worker boards after their starting date
scenario: Tom posts an unfilled weekly pharmacist vacancy running for several weeks. Once its starting date passes, Sara cannot find the remaining dates on the public board. Omar likewise loses an equivalent recurring vacancy from the community board.
test_needed: Create an unassigned recurring slot starting yesterday with a future occurrence and assert it remains discoverable on worker boards.

owner_question.question: When Tom's recurring vacancy has future unfilled dates but its starting date has passed, what should Sara see?
options: The remaining future dates
A new advertisement Tom must publish for each date
No vacancy after the starting date passes (keep today's behaviour)

title: Public boards compare local shift times against the UTC clock
scenario: Tom posts a Sydney shift ending at 5 pm. At 6 pm Sydney time, Sara can still find and express interest in it because the board compares its ending time with the much earlier UTC clock.
test_needed: Freeze time at 6 pm Sydney time and assert a same-day shift ending at 5 pm is absent from both public lists.

owner_question.question: At 6 pm in Tom's pharmacy, should Sara still see a shift that ended there at 5 pm?
options: Hide it using the pharmacy's local time
Show it as closed and prevent applications
Keep it open until the UTC comparison expires (keep today's behaviour)

title: Accepting a valid counter offer for a vacancy without dated slots crashes
scenario: Tom posts a full-time vacancy without dated shifts. Sara submits a counter offer containing the requested working times but no date, which the app accepts. When Tom accepts it, the request fails instead of sending Sara an offer.
test_needed: Submit a valid slotless counter offer without slot_date, then accept it and assert a controlled successful response instead of an exception.

owner_question.question: When Sara counters Tom's full-time vacancy without dated shifts, what should accepting it do?
options: Send Sara an offer without requiring a shift date
Require a date before allowing the counter offer submission
Leave the submitted counter offer unacceptable (keep today's behaviour)

title: Confirming one recurring date books dates outside the accepted terms
scenario: Sara counters for just one date in Tom's recurring vacancy, and Tom accepts that date. Sara reviews terms describing that date and confirms. When the booking is finalized, the app assigns Sara to every unfilled date in the recurring series, including dates she did not accept.
test_needed: Confirm an offer targeting one recurring occurrence and assert no assignments exist for any other occurrence.

owner_question.question: When Sara accepts terms for one date in Tom's recurring vacancy, which dates should she be booked for?
options: Only the date she accepted
The whole series after separately reviewing and accepting every date
Every unfilled recurring date immediately (keep today's behaviour)

title: Public shift responses expose other workers' names and email addresses.
scenario: Tom posts a public shift with several vacancies, and Ben confirms one while payment is pending. Sara browses that shift without joining Tom's pharmacy. The response reveals Ben's name and email; it also exposes contact details for workers already assigned.
test_needed: Retrieve a public shift as unrelated Sara and assert Ben's pending-payment and assignment contact details are absent.

owner_question.question: When Sara browses Tom's public vacancy, whose contact details should she see?
options: Only her own; Tom's managers can see other candidates
Confirmed coworkers' details after Sara is booked
Every candidate's details while browsing (keep today's behaviour)

title: Confirmed counteroffers are invoiced using the original shift hours.
scenario: Tom advertises a flexible shift from 09:00 to 17:00. Sara proposes 10:00 to 14:00, Tom accepts, and Sara confirms. Her booking retains the original hours, and its invoice preview charges Tom for eight hours instead of the agreed four.
test_needed: Confirm a 10:00–14:00 counteroffer against a 09:00–17:00 slot and assert the booking and invoice use four hours.

owner_question.question: After Tom and Sara agree to shorten the shift, which hours should her booking and invoice use?
options: The agreed 10:00–14:00 hours
Require Tom to amend the vacancy before confirmation
The original 09:00–17:00 hours (keep today's behaviour)

title: Confirming one recurring occurrence books the worker for the entire series.
scenario: Tom posts a recurring Monday vacancy. Sara proposes working only the second Monday, and Tom accepts that date. When Sara confirms, she is assigned every Monday in the series, including dates she never accepted.
test_needed: Confirm an offer for the second of three recurring Mondays and assert no assignments exist for the other Mondays.

owner_question.question: When Sara accepts only the second Monday of Tom's recurring vacancy, what should be booked?
options: Only the accepted Monday
Require explicit acceptance of every date together
Every occurrence automatically (keep today's behaviour)

title: Upcoming bookings appear in completed-work history.
scenario: Tom books Sara for next week. Before Sara works the shift, both Tom's history and Sara's history already include it. Their completed-work lists therefore contain future commitments alongside past work.
test_needed: Create only a future assigned shift and assert both manager and worker history endpoints exclude it.

owner_question.question: Should Tom and Sara see next week's confirmed booking in History?
options: Only after the shift ends
In a separate clearly labelled upcoming section
Alongside completed work immediately (keep today's behaviour)

title: Shift lifecycle filters compare pharmacy clock times with UTC.
scenario: Sara finishes Tom's Sydney shift at 17:00. At 20:00 Sydney time, the filters compare its finish against the UTC morning clock and still classify it as upcoming. Tom and Sara continue seeing an ended booking as confirmed, and ended vacancies can remain active.
test_needed: Freeze time at 20:00 Sydney time for a same-day 17:00 finish and assert the shift is excluded from upcoming and active results.

owner_question.question: When Tom's pharmacy clock passes the shift's finish time, when should Sara's booking leave Upcoming?
options: At the finish time in that pharmacy's timezone
After a defined grace period in that pharmacy's timezone
